key_insight: Conditioning a recurrent forecasting model on temperature and thermal rate enables accurate prediction of grain size distribution evolution during non-isothermal heat treatment.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on costly grain-growth simulations when evaluating heat-treatment schedules for polycrystalline materials.
method: Encode grain size distributions with a convolutional neural network.
Embed instantaneous temperature and thermal rate with a dedicated multilayer perceptron.
Forecast temporal evolution with a recurrent network trained on validated front-tracking simulations.
evidence_signal: Across simulated thermal paths, k-fold cross-validation yielded mean relative errors of 2.99% for one-hour cycles and 4.51% for four-hour cycles with R² > 0.99; ten simulations spanning four unseen thermal histories yielded errors of 1.91%–14.66%.
watch_item: Evaluation uses simulation-generated data, and higher errors on some unseen thermal histories warrant caution when extrapolating to new heat-treatment schedules.
paper_title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
